podcast.body: Noel Gallagher, as the chief songwriter, is estimated to earn £3,000 per day in royalties from "Wonderwall." This significant income highlights the song's enduring popularity and its substantial financial impact, a factor noted in the financial dynamics surrounding the band's reunion. "It's estimated that Noel makes 3,000 pounds a day just from Wonderwall."

podcast.body: Originally titled "Wishing Stone," the meaning of this song has evolved over time; initially about Noel Gallagher's then-girlfriend Meg Matthews, it later morphed into being about an imaginary savior and was even connected to George Harrison's 1968 album "Wonder Wall Music." Written quickly in the months leading up to the "What's the Story Morning Glory" album, Noel sought a stripped-down vibe inspired by Portishead's "Dummy." Recorded at Rockfield Studios in rural Wales in May 1995 over half a day, the title may also refer to a brick wall on the studio grounds where Noel would sit and strum his guitar. Noel played guitar and bass, Alan White provided a shuffling groove, and producer Owen Morris added intensity with "brick walling," a cello, and a four-note piano motif. Liam Gallagher chose to sing this song over "Don't Look Back In Anger." It was first heard backstage at Glastonbury on June 24, 1995, for a BBC TV special and was performed sporadically that summer. Released as the fourth single from "Morning Glory," it reached number two in the UK, number one in Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, and number eight on the Billboard Hot 100 in the US, where it was the number one alternative song. "Noll once told me that he makes about 3,000 pounds a day from the song."
